note: Mississippi River bottomland forest on the New Madrid Bend, reached on county gravel roads off Route WW and Route AB. The area map marks about a dozen primitive camp sites, each by a small parking lot; this pin is the northernmost, a small pull-off at a field corner on a detached tract off the county road, and others sit along the river road by Dawson and Round Holes and through the main forest off Route AB. Large parts of the area flood. Spot length is not published. --Claude
summary: Confirmed MDC 'Designated Camping Sites, Individual Campsites'; brochure 'Primitive camping is permitted in designated areas... Camping is allowed on or adjacent to parking lots, unless otherwise posted', 14 days in 30. Map (11/9/2023) has 12 Primitive Camp Site symbols, each with a P. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights written manual. Pin (GIS 1052) is the northernmost, minor spot: a small pull-off at a field corner on a detached tract. One split proposed for the main-forest camps off Route AB (6.6 km SE). Not waterfront kept for the pin; a river-road camp (1048) on the Mississippi bank is a lead if the pin ever moves. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: area page 'Camping: Open Camping - Walk-in/Float-in/Backpack, Designated Camping Sites, Individual Campsites'. Brochure: 'Primitive camping is permitted in designated areas. Walk-in camping is allowed, EXCEPT during all deer and turkey seasons. Camping is allowed on or adjacent to parking lots, unless otherwise posted. Campers are limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period... Motor vehicles and horseback riding are allowed on public roadways and in parking areas.' The map marks 12 'Primitive Camp Site' symbols, each beside a P, and GIS has 12 camping points (4 typed 'Designated Camping Area'). Designated drive-in spots, so it stays. Imagery: the pin spot is a small grassy/gravel apron (~15 x 15 m) at a bend of a gravel county road at a field corner; camp 618 is a ~25 m clearing on a spur off Route AB with a vehicle parked; 1051 is a pull-in at a road corner. A 23-ft rig fits each; they are road-side pull-offs, not developed sites. Area page: 'This department area is closed during periods of high water'; 'During seasonal flooding, large portions or all of the area may not be accessible.' No ford, 4WD or rig wording.

PIN (minor spot): stored 36.59477,-89.45611 = GIS 1052 / lot 7384, the northernmost camp, on a detached tract at a field corner on the county road north of the main area. There is no single main camp: the spots are spread over ~9 km. If AWH prefers the river-road group, GIS 1053 / lot 730 (36.5707,-89.4765, by Dawson Hole and the non-concrete boat ramp) is central to the north part.

SPLIT proposed (1): 'Donaldson Point Conservation Area (Route AB camps)' at 36.5456,-89.4143 (GIS 618 / lot 734, camp #5 by Bowman Hole, first camp on the spur off Route AB), state/MDC, same groups, phone 573-748-5134, not waterfront (in forest). It is 6.6 km SE of the pin and reached from Route AB rather than the WW/404 county roads; the other seven main-forest camps (1045-1047, 1049, 615-617) are 0.7-3 km from it on the same MDC roads. No existing entry within 3 km of any main-forest camp (campgrounds.json checked).

WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront, kept for the pin): the pin is at a field corner ~2 km from the river. Lead, not this pin: camp 1048 (36.5652,-89.4725) sits at the edge of the river road on the Mississippi bank, the water ~25-30 m west across a bare, sparsely treed bank with no road between; it would need the full gate (and the road at the point itself may be the problem) if it ever became an entry's pin.
Season (manual, year-round with the high-water note) left as stored.
